repository_projection.activation_rule: P20-T02 must change this projection to 4.0.0 and regenerate every coordinated manifest in one governed change; no current manifest value is product-version authority.

semver_rules.breaking_semantic_or_api_change: Increment MAJOR when a Supported semantic guarantee, source API, machine contract, or compatibility promise is removed or incompatibly changed.
semver_rules.backward_compatible_feature: Increment MINOR for an additive feature that preserves every Supported contract in the current major line.
semver_rules.backward_compatible_fix: Increment PATCH for a correction that restores documented Supported behavior without adding or removing a compatibility guarantee.
semver_rules.documentation_only_correction: No product version change is required when normative meaning, public metadata, install behavior, and generated artifacts are unchanged; record an erratum when the corrected text was public.
semver_rules.target_profile_data_update: A profile-only fact correction uses the profile's independent version; also change product SemVer when the shipped compiler behavior or a public product support promise changes.
semver_rules.security_fix: Use PATCH when compatible, MINOR for an additive mitigation, and MAJOR for an unavoidable incompatible Supported-contract change; an advisory does not waive certification or publication authorization.
semver_rules.packaging_only_fix: Use PATCH for a new immutable public package that corrects installation or packaging; never replace an already published coordinate.

target_profile_policy.minimum_supported_versions: The minimum is the lowest exact engine/profile identity carrying a current Supported claim: PCRE2 10.42, ECMAScript 2024 under its registered host evidence, and CPython re 3.11 text/bytes. This does not imply intervening or later implementations.
target_profile_policy.tested_ranges: Support is an enumerated set of exact governed profile and runtime identities, not an open-ended version range. A range may be published only when every covered compatibility class has representative governed evidence and the policy explicitly registers the range.
target_profile_policy.newer_versions: A newly released or newer upstream engine is unknown and unsupported until facts are reviewed, a profile is added or revised, and required certification passes; latest is never a profile alias.
target_profile_policy.eol_versions: An EOL upstream version may remain Supported only with an explicit security/maintenance owner and evidence path; otherwise it is downgraded to Legacy or removed under deprecation policy.
target_profile_policy.prerelease_engines: Nightly, alpha, beta, and release-candidate engines are unsupported unless separately registered as Preview with exact immutable identity and evidence; they cannot satisfy stable Supported certification.
target_profile_policy.profile_revisions: Profile revisions use their own SemVer and may refine target facts, capability status, diagnostics, or lowering within specification authority. Shipped behavior/support changes also trigger product SemVer as classified by product policy.
target_profile_policy.uncertainty: Unlisted capabilities remain unknown, unsupported behavior is explicit, and compilation must never silently degrade semantic intent.

runtime_platform_policy.supported: A runtime/platform/architecture is Supported only within an exact support claim whose install and execution path participates in required release certification. Toolchain constraints are eligibility declarations, not support evidence by themselves.
runtime_platform_policy.known_compatible_uncertified: Observed or declared compatibility without a required certification row is labeled known-compatible but uncertified; it is non-blocking evidence and cannot be marketed as Supported.
runtime_platform_policy.preview: A Preview runtime/platform has a registered bounded claim and disclosed gaps; regressions block release only when they also violate an explicitly required certification operation or another Supported contract.
runtime_platform_policy.unsupported: Any runtime, platform, browser, operating-system version, or architecture outside an exact registered claim is unsupported, even if local builds happen to pass.
runtime_platform_policy.architectures: Architecture support is never inherited from an operating-system family. Current public claims are x86_64 only where explicitly stated; arm64 and other architectures remain unsupported until registered and certified.
runtime_platform_policy.deferred_toolchains: A deferred or unpinned build/package-manager tool in toolchain.json cannot establish a public Supported claim. P20-T02 must either pin/qualify it for publication or preserve the affected Preview/unsupported boundary.

A breaking semantic change requires a new specification major and product major when shipped as the default Supported behavior.
Supported Simply entrypoints receive source/API and semantic compatibility within a product major.
Additive helpers may be minor; incompatible signature or meaning changes are major.
The frontend preserves its explicit dialect and uncertainty contracts.
New diagnostics or safer rejection may be patch/minor only when existing documented successful semantics remain compatible.
Documented Supported public entrypoints receive source compatibility within a product major.
Binary compatibility exists only for an explicitly registered ABI/platform range.
Semantic intent is governed by specification/profile identity; serialized shape is governed by its contract version.
Pattern text and runtime options remain distinct; capability uncertainty never silently degrades.
Documented commands, option meanings, exit statuses, and declared JSON are compatible within a major.
Human prose, spacing, and color are not machine APIs unless explicitly designated.
Compatibility follows the schema/protocol's own version policy.
A breaking public schema/protocol change also requires an appropriate product major when used by a Supported surface.
Guarantees apply only within each registered tier/platform/runtime scope.
Bindings cannot claim compatibility with a canonical-core product version outside the explicit release mapping.
The VS Code/LSP surface is Preview and independently versioned.
Its manifest/release notes must state the exact compatible STRling product range before publication.

deprecation.notice: Document the deprecated surface, first deprecated product release, affected support tiers, and removal target in release notes and the canonical API/reference documentation.
deprecation.minimum_window: For Supported surfaces, retain through at least one subsequent MINOR release and never remove before the next MAJOR; a calendar duration alone is insufficient.
deprecation.replacement: Provide a supported replacement or explicit migration path and mechanically test it before removal.
deprecation.removal: Removal requires the announced boundary, a breaking-change classification, release notes, and a major product version when a Supported compatibility guarantee is broken.
deprecation.emergency: A severe security, legal, or data-integrity risk may require immediate disablement; record the evidence, owner decision, advisory, migration guidance, and SemVer impact.

release_candidate.promotion: Stable must use the same exact source commit as the terminal RC. Version-only package metadata changes are generated from policy, and stable artifacts are rebuilt, compared for allowed coordinate-only differences, and fully re-certified.
release_candidate.source_identity: RC evidence binds the exact source SHA, generated state, toolchain/profile identities, package subjects, checksums, SBOMs, provenance, environment, and waivers.
release_candidate.change_rule: Any source change, governed input change, dependency/lock change, generated-output change, artifact-content change beyond approved coordinate metadata, or waiver change requires a new monotonically numbered RC and fresh required certification.
release_candidate.evidence_binding: No evidence may be transferred between candidates unless the governing producer explicitly authenticates identical inputs and policy permits reuse; Release remains no-reuse where registered.

covered_actions: Production release tag creation or push
Any public prerelease or stable coordinate
publication.tooling_guard: Local, Pull Request, Full, and Release profiles always have publication=false. P20-T02 may build, inspect, and dry-run; P20-T04 may prepare and certify; only an explicitly owner-authorized P20-T05 run may cross the protected publication boundary.

Keep the release in published-but-unverified state until all required public checks pass

A waiver never grants publication authorization
